chapter_name: Chapter 02: Tenses and Their Functional Uses
learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will understand the functional differences between confusing tense pairs (e.g., Simple Past vs. Present Perfect, Past Simple vs. Past Perfect) to accurately express time relations.]
warm_up_hook: ⏳ Ready to time travel? Tenses are the time-machines of English grammar. One wrong gear, and you might accidentally say you are STILL doing your homework from 2018! Let's master the timeline! 🚀

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Simple Past is for finished actions at a specific time in the past. Present Perfect connects the past to the present (actions happening at an unspecified time, or past actions with present consequences).
examples_or_templates: Simple Past: I lost my keys yesterday. (Action finished, time is stated)
Present Perfect: I have lost my keys. (I don't have them right now; effect is present)

lesson_modules.teaching_content: When telling a story about the past, if you need to refer to something that happened even EARLIER, use the Past Perfect (had + V3). It shows which action happened first.
examples_or_templates: Past Perfect: When I arrived at the station (Action 2), the train had left (Action 1).

lesson_modules.teaching_content: The future isn't just 'will'. We use 'going to' for planned intentions and evidence-based predictions. We use Present Continuous for fixed, scheduled arrangements in the near future.
examples_or_templates: Going to: Look at those dark clouds! It is going to rain. (Evidence)
Present Continuous: I am meeting the dentist at 3 PM tomorrow. (Fixed arrangement)

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Which tense correctly completes this sentence? 'I _____ him since we graduated.'
❓ Complete the sentence showing sequence of past events: 'By the time the firemen arrived, the fire _____.'

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Fill in the blanks with the correct past tense (Simple or Perfect): 'The teacher _____ (be) angry because the students _____ (not/do) their homework.'
subjective_practice.hint: Which action happened first? Not doing the homework happened before the teacher got angry.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Rewrite this sentence using 'going to' instead of 'will' and explain why it might be more appropriate: 'My bags are packed; I will travel to Paris tomorrow.'
subjective_practice.hint: Think about pre-planned intentions versus spontaneous decisions.

activity_or_assignment.title: 🎬 The Alibi
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Imagine you are a detective interrogating a suspect. Write a short dialogue (6-8 lines). The suspect must use the Past Perfect tense to explain what they 'had done' before a specific crime occurred.

chapter_summary: ⭐ Use Simple Past for finished actions with specific time; Present Perfect when the past affects the present.
⭐ Past Perfect (had + V3) highlights the older of two past actions.
⭐ Future intentions and fixed plans often use 'going to' or Present Continuous, not just 'will'.
